souks_page.hero_subtitle: Everyday medina markets and narrow streets for spices, produce and local El Jadida life.
souks_page.overview.title: Markets inside the walls
souks_page.overview.p1: El Jadida’s souks are working markets more than tourist bazaars: produce, spices, household goods and the daily traffic of the medina.
souks_page.overview.p2: Morning is liveliest. Bargain politely where expected, keep bags close, and step aside for carts in narrow lanes.
souks_page.overview.p3: Use the souks as the connective tissue between the Portuguese monuments, the Mellah and the port.

souks_page.faq.title: Medina Souks FAQ
souks_page.faq.q1.question: Touristy or local?
souks_page.faq.q1.answer: Mostly local everyday shopping with some visitor traffic near the monuments.
souks_page.faq.q2.question: Best time?
souks_page.faq.q2.answer: Morning for full stalls and energy.
souks_page.faq.q3.question: What to buy?
souks_page.faq.q3.answer: Spices, olives, simple crafts — nothing you cannot find elsewhere, but the setting is the point.
souks_page.faq.q4.question: Cash only?
souks_page.faq.q5.question: Easy to navigate?
souks_page.faq.q5.answer: Yes on a short loop; ask a shopkeeper if you lose the main arteries.
